2027-07-24.title: Third Saturday of Kaitha
2027-07-24.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Whoever is not against you is for you
2027-07-24.alt: Season of Kaitha (Qaita, Summer), which began on Sunday 4 July with the Feast of the Twelve Apostles: the season of the Church's growth and harvest, when the Church remembers the apostles and martyrs who watered her field with their blood and keeps herself ready for the coming of the Lord. The calendar's own headings: “Boasting is evil”; “He that is not against you is for you”. In the Latin and Syro-Malankara calendars today is the memory of Saint Sharbel Makhluf, a monk and hermit of the Maronite Church of Lebanon.
2027-07-24.verse: Instead you ought to say, “If the Lord wishes, we will live and do this or that.”
theo: Saint James paints a scene from the market. A trader says, “Today or tomorrow we will go to such and such a town and spend a year there, doing business and making money.” There is nothing wrong with planning, and James does not forbid it. What he exposes is the presumption in the plan, the tone of a man who speaks as if he were the lord of tomorrow. “Yet you do not even know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? For you are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.” Anyone who has seen the morning mist on the hills of Idukki or Munnar in the monsoon knows how quickly it is gone when the sun rises. The psalmist prays the same truth: “So teach us to count our days that we may gain a wise heart” (Psalm 90:12). Then comes the remedy: “Instead you ought to say, ‘If the Lord wishes, we will live and do this or that.’” Many Kerala families keep the habit in their speech: ‘if God helps’. It is not a phrase to excuse laziness; it is the confession that every plan is made inside God's providence. “The human mind plans the way, but the Lord directs the steps” (Proverbs 16:9).

James adds two sharp sentences. “As it is, you boast in your arrogance; all such boasting is evil.” And then the line that every conscience hears: “Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, commits sin.” The Church teaches that sin is not only what we do but also what we fail to do, in thought, word, deed and omission. Every good examination of conscience asks not only what we have done but what we have left undone. The man in James's market had no plan to harm anyone. His fault was that God and the neighbour did not appear in the plan at all: the good he could do today he put off for a tomorrow that he does not own.

The Gospel begins with a small quarrel among the apostles. John says, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow with us.” It is the voice of the group: he is not one of us. Jesus answers, “Do not stop him; for whoever is not against you is for you.” The same breadth of heart was in Moses when Joshua wished to silence Eldad and Medad, who were prophesying in the camp: “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the Lord's people were prophets” (Numbers 11:29). The Church teaches, of course, that the fullness of the means of salvation is found in the Catholic Church. But she also teaches that “many elements of sanctification and of truth” are found outside her visible boundaries (Catechism 819), and that good done in the name of Christ by others is not to be forbidden with envy. This is the same lesson as on Tuesday: the spirit of rivalry is the opposite of the wisdom from above.

Then the Gospel turns toward the Cross: “When the days drew near for him to be taken up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem.” Isaiah's servant had said, “I have set my face like flint” (Isaiah 50:7). Jesus sends messengers ahead to a Samaritan village, and the villagers do not receive him because his face is set toward Jerusalem. James and John, whom the Lord called Sons of Thunder (Mark 3:17), say, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from heaven and consume them?” They remember Elijah, who once called down fire (2 Kings 1:10), and the Church has met this prophet more than once this week. But Jesus “turned and rebuked them. Then they went on to another village.” No fire, no argument, no revenge. He who has set his face to the Cross moves on to another village. It is the way of the Lamb. In many homes Saturday is kept in honour of the Mother of the Lord, and in her we see the opposite of the arrogant plan: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word” (Luke 1:38). Her whole life was an ‘if the Lord wishes’.
outline: A mist on the hills in the morning: our plans and the Lord who directs the steps.
Plan, but with the words “If the Lord wishes”; the good not done is sin.
Point 2 · Whoever is not against you
The spirit of the group against the breadth of Jesus; good done in his name.
Point 3 · His face set toward Jerusalem
No fire from heaven; the Lamb moves on to the next village.
“If the Lord wishes, we will live and do this or that.”
live: Before each important plan this week, say quietly: “If the Lord wishes”, and offer the plan to him. Do today the good thing that you have been putting off.
Welcome a good done by another (Luke 9:50)
Find one good work done by someone outside your own group, parish or association, and thank God for it and for the people who do it.
fathers: James does not forbid us to make plans but teaches us to refer every plan to the will of God, who holds our life in his hand; the one who forgets God in his plans builds on a mist.
Patience belongs to Christ; the disciple of the Lamb overcomes by gentleness, not by revenge.
magis: Death is the end of man's earthly pilgrimage, of the time of grace and mercy which God offers him; there is no return to another earthly life, and so we must be watchful.
Sins can be classed in thought, word, deed or omission (compare James 4:17: to know the good and not do it is sin).
Many elements of sanctification and truth are found outside the visible structure of the Catholic Church; the Spirit of Christ uses them as means of salvation, and they call us toward unity.
saints: Third Saturday of Kaitha; in many homes Saturday is Mary's day. In the Latin and Syro-Malankara calendars, Saint Sharbel Makhluf (1828–1898), a monk and hermit of the Maronite Church in Lebanon, much loved by many Indian Catholics.

19–24 July: the third week of Kaitha. Mon 19 to Wed 21 and Sat 24: the Third Week of Kaitha, with the Epistle from the Letter of James (Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat). Thu 22: Saint Mary Magdalene, apostle of the apostles, with readings of her own. Fri 23: the Third Friday of Kaitha (readings from the 2022–23 calendar, verify locally). Sat 24: in the Latin and Malankara calendars, Saint Sharbel Makhluf, a monk of the Maronite Church. Looking ahead: the Fourth Sunday of Kaitha on 25 July, and Saint Alphonsa on Wednesday 28 July.
2027-07-24.prayer: Lord God, our lives are like a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes, and our tomorrows are in your hands. Teach us to count our days and gain a wise heart. Let us make our plans in humility and say with sincere hearts, “If the Lord wishes.” Keep us from boasting, and move us to do today the good that we know. Give us the breadth of heart of Jesus, who did not forbid the stranger who cast out demons in his name; and give us his gentleness, who set his face toward Jerusalem and refused to call down fire. Through Mary, who said “Let it be with me according to your word”, and through Christ our Lord, who with you and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Lamb of God who set his face toward Jerusalem makes present his one offering, and we place before him all our plans and our tomorrows. We receive the Bread of the journey, and we are sent out to do the good we know, in the company of all who work in his name.

quick: James: our life is a mist; say “If the Lord wishes”; boasting is evil; to know the good and not do it is sin.

Luke: John tries to stop someone who is not of their group, and Jesus says whoever is not against you is for you; Jesus sets his face toward Jerusalem and rebukes his disciples who want to call down fire.
Together: humility in our plans, breadth in our hearts, gentleness toward those who refuse us.
2027-07-24.action: Offer one plan this week to God with the words “If the Lord wishes”, and do one good thing you have been putting off.
2027-07-24.question: What good do I know and still not do, and whom do I try to stop because he is not one of us?

family.explain: In the morning the mist on the hills is thick, but when the sun comes up it vanishes. Saint James says that our life is like that, and so we should say, “If God wishes”, when we plan something. Then Jesus' friend John saw a man doing good in Jesus' name and told him to stop, because he was not in their group. Jesus said: do not stop him! Whoever is not against us is for us. God is happy when anybody does good.
family.intention: We thank God for all the good people we know, even if they do not belong to our group, and we pray for those who are in trouble.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we thank for doing good in our village, and how?”

illus: In a town parish (a story told to illustrate the reading) some members of the choir complained that a group of young people from another parish were teaching the Our Father and a few songs to street children near the bus stand. ‘They are not ours,’ they said. The old vicar went and sat on the bench to listen. The children were saying the Our Father, the same prayer the parish teaches in its own catechism class. He came back and said, ‘Whoever is not against us is for us.’ In the next rains, when the bus stand was flooded, he lent the young people the parish hall for the classes, and the choir members brought tea.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you set your face toward Jerusalem and you did not call down fire. Make our plans humble and our hearts wide. Amen.
share: You are a mist that appears for a little while (James 4:14). How do I live as one who is only passing through?
If the Lord wishes (James 4:15). What plan do I need to offer to him today?
Anyone who knows the right thing to do and fails to do it commits sin (James 4:17). What good do I know, and not do?
Do not stop him; for whoever is not against you is for you (Luke 9:50). Whom do I try to stop because he is not one of us?
pm.resp: Lord, make our hearts wide and our plans humble.
interc: For the Church, that she may rejoice in every good done in the name of Christ.
For those who plan our towns and villages, that they may plan with humility and care for the poor.
For all who are tempted to answer refusal with anger, that they may follow the gentleness of the Lamb.
For those who think they have many tomorrows, that they may do the good that they can do today.
For ourselves, that we may say “If the Lord wishes” and mean it.
pm.close: Father, our days are in your hands. Teach us to count them wisely, and to follow your Son who set his face toward Jerusalem. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, you have seen the mist on the hills in the morning. It is thick, and then it is gone. Saint James says that our life is like that: “You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes” (James 4:14).

So he gives us a lesson: when we plan, we should say, “If the Lord wishes, we will live and do this or that” (James 4:15). We may plan, but we are not the lords of tomorrow. And he adds a sentence for each of us: “Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, commits sin” (James 4:17). What good do you know and keep putting off?

In the Gospel John tells Jesus: “We tried to stop him, because he does not follow with us.” Jesus replies: “Do not stop him; for whoever is not against you is for you” (Luke 9:49–50). God is glad when anyone does good in his name. Let us not be jealous of other people's good works.

Then Jesus sets his face toward Jerusalem. A village refuses him, and James and John want fire from heaven. Jesus rebukes them, and they go on to another village (Luke 9:55–56). The Lord is gentle; he does not take revenge, because he is going to the Cross for us.
This week let us offer our plans to God, do one good thing that we have put off, and say a thank-you for someone's good work. Amen.
kids: Children, have you seen mist on the hills? In the morning it is thick and white, and then the sun comes and it is gone! Our life is like that, so we must always do good today and say, “If God wishes.” And if you see someone who is not your friend doing good, do not stop them: clap for them! Jesus says: whoever is not against us is for us.

intro: Theme: “Instead you ought to say, ‘If the Lord wishes, we will live and do this or that.’”
A life like a mist, a heart as wide as the Lord's, and a face set toward Jerusalem without fire from heaven.

sub: Plans made as if we owned tomorrow.
The good we know and do not do.
q: So teach us to count our days that we may gain a wise heart.
Yet you do not even know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? For you are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
points.apply: Offer one plan to the Lord this week, and do one good you have put off.

sub: Good done in Christ's name is not to be forbidden.
q: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit on them!”
But Jesus said to him, “Do not stop him; for whoever is not against you is for you.”
points.apply: Thank God this week for a good work done by people outside your own group.

sub: The servant who sets his face like flint.
A village refuses; the sons of thunder want fire.
The Lamb rebukes them and moves on.
q: The Lord God helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
When the days drew near for him to be taken up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem.
points.apply: When someone refuses or hurts you this week, answer with patience and move on.

concl: Our lives are in the Lord's hands; we plan with humility and do the good we know.
His heart is wide, and his gentleness is the way of the Lamb on the road to the Cross.
2027-07-24.resolve: This week, say “If the Lord wishes” over every plan, do one good thing now, and bless the good that others do.
